title: Stacking machine learning on habitat MRI predicts cervical cancer lymph node metastasis
summary: In 623 early-stage cervical cancer patients (311 training, 187 internal validation, 125 external validation), a stacking ensemble of five base classifiers with an XGBoost meta-model used intratumoral and peritumoral habitat radiomics from T2, DWI and contrast-enhanced MRI plus clinicopathological variables. The best base learner reached AUC 0.845 externally and the meta-learner 0.875, significantly higher than base learners and unimodal approaches.
ai_technology: Stacking ensemble (logistic regression, XGBoost, Elastic Net, attention CNN, SVM; XGBoost meta-model) on habitat radiomics

evidence.tested: Training, internal validation and external validation cohorts (n=623 total).
evidence.unknown: Retrospective with prospective validation described but not detailed; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning ensemble predicts lymph node metastasis before surgery.
